London, 30<sup>th</sup> April 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**President Barack Obama** said he is hopeful that Chrysler LLC will be able to forge an alliance with Fiat as it prepares for bankruptcy.  The president’s staff is aiming for Chrysler to file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection as early as today to pave the way for Fiat to take a 20 percent stake in Chrysler. Chrysler’s best assets would be sold to a new entity that would have an ownership structure similar to that envisioned in an out-of-court deal between the U.S. automaker and Fiat.  Administration officials were still resolving outstanding issues and the plan wasn’t finished. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**General Motors Corp.’s** bondholders plan to present a counteroffer to President Barack Obama’s auto task force in Washington today that would give them control of the carmaker.  The bondholder committee plans to reject GM’s April 27 debt exchange offer that asked them to swap all their claims for a 10 percent stake in the reorganized automaker. GM has said 90% of bondholders owning $27 billion must tender their holdings by June 1 or it will be forced to file for a government-supported bankruptcy. The counteroffer proposes that bondholders and a United Auto Workers retiree-medical fund both exchange all their claims for equity.   GM bondholders are proposing they get a 51 % stake in the reorganized carmaker, the healthcare fund get a 41 % share, and common shareholders get 1 %. This structure would enable the U.S. Treasury to be paid back and avoid nationalization of GM. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**Total refined platinum output by Anglo Platinum** declined by 5,7% y-o-y in Q109, while the company’s plans to produce 2,4Moz  of platinum this year remained firmly in place.  Platinum output fell to 404 000 oz in Q109, a 52% decline on Q408.  The decline was mainly as a result of maintenance shutdowns at its Waterval and Polokwane smelters.   These shutdowns had also resulted in declining palladium and nickel production, with palladium output dropping by 47,8% quarter-on-quarter and 4,4% year-on-year to 231 100 oz. Rhodium production, which had a longer processing time, had not been impacted on by the shutdowns,and was up by 28,1% q-o-q to 73 800 oz.  This was, however, a 31% year-on-year decline in rhodium production.  Angloplat reported that it had reduced its headcount by nearly 4 200 employees, in Q109.  The producer had also cut output at its Mogalakwena mine by 50% for cost-cutting measures.  Similarly, the process to suspend mining operations at the Blesbok shaft, at its Siphumelele mine, had started.  Cash operating costs declined by 7%/oz in the quarter.  Progress had been made with the operational restructuring of the Rustenburg operations, which now consists of five separate mines, and the Amandelbult operations, which now consists of two separate mines. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Zimplats** has secured a R300m loan from a South African bank to complete its Ngezi e

xpansion project, overcoming concerns that it would not be able to finance the end stages of the project.  The commissioning of the new Ngezi concentrator has been delayed for a month due to late delivery of equipment. The expansion project is still expected to be completed within the approved budget of $340m.   Once completed, it will boost Zimplats’ production to 180,000 ounces of platinum/yr, compared to current output of about 95,000oz.  Zimplats posted a profit of $1.1m, up from an operating loss of over $11m.  Total ore mined was 23% lower than the previous quarter, due to the closure of open pit mining operations in November 2008. _Source:  Mining Mx_ 

**ETF Securities** said that holdings in its London platinum and palladium exchange-traded commodities (ETCs) rose by 2.4% and 4.4 % respectively last week.  The company confirmed that the amount of metal it uses to back its PHPT.L platinum ETC increased by 8,000 oz to 347,596 oz in the week to 24th April.  In addition, the London-based ETC specialist - which has assets worth about $9.6 billion - saw holdings in its palladium-backed product (PHPD.L) increase roughly 11,000 oz to 262,973 oz. _Source:  Reuters_
